-------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m8p1t0 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Clerks, Sections, MaxVer

Depts == {"arts", "sciences"}
DeptOf == [s \in Sections |-> IF s <= 2 THEN "arts" ELSE "sciences"]

NoOne == "unlocked"
NoSnap == [sec |-> 0, base |-> 0]

VARIABLES deptLock, secLock, ver, snap, downClerks

vars == <<deptLock, secLock, ver, snap, downClerks>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ deptLock \in [Depts -> Clerks \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ secLock \in [Sections -> Clerks \cup {NoOne}]
    /\ ver \in [Sections -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ snap \in [Clerks -> [sec : Sections \cup {0}, base : 0..MaxVer]]
    /\ downClerks \subseteq Clerks

HoldsDept(c) == \E d \in Depts : deptLock[d] = c
HoldsSec(c) == \E s \in Sections : secLock[s] = c

Init ==
    /\ deptLock = [d \in Depts |-> NoOne]
    /\ secLock = [s \in Sections |-> NoOne]
    /\ ver = [s \in Sections |-> 0]
    /\ snap = [c \in Clerks |-> NoSnap]
    /\ downClerks = {}

TakeDept(c, d) ==
    /\ c \notin downClerks
    /\ deptLock[d] = NoOne
    /\ ~HoldsDept(c)
    /\ deptLock' = [deptLock EXCEPT ![d] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<secLock, ver, snap, downClerks>>

TakeSection(c, s) ==
    /\ c \notin downClerks
    /\ deptLock[DeptOf[s]] = c
    /\ secLock[s] = NoOne
    /\ ~HoldsSec(c)
    /\ secLock' = [secLock EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deptLock, ver, snap, downClerks>>

Snapshot(c, s) ==
    /\ c \notin downClerks
    /\ secLock[s] = c
    /\ snap[c] = NoSnap
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = [sec |-> s, base |-> ver[s]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deptLock, secLock, ver, downClerks>>

Commit(c) ==
    /\ c \notin downClerks
    /\ snap[c] # NoSnap
    /\ LET s == snap[c].sec IN
       /\ secLock[s] = c
       /\ snap[c].base = ver[s]
       /\ ver[s] < MaxVer
       /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
       /\ secLock' = [secLock EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
       /\ deptLock' = [d \in Depts |-> IF deptLock[d] = c THEN NoOne ELSE deptLock[d]]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoSnap]
    /\ UNCHANGED downClerks

CrashSilently(c) ==
    /\ c \notin downClerks
    /\ downClerks' = downClerks \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deptLock, secLock, ver, snap>>

ReclaimFrom(c) ==
    /\ c \in downClerks
    /\ (HoldsDept(c) \/ HoldsSec(c) \/ snap[c] # NoSnap)
    /\ deptLock' = [d \in Depts |-> IF deptLock[d] = c THEN NoOne ELSE deptLock[d]]
    /\ secLock' = [s \in Sections |-> IF secLock[s] = c THEN NoOne ELSE secLock[s]]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoSnap]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, downClerks>>

Reboot(c) ==
    /\ c \in downClerks
    /\ ~HoldsDept(c) /\ ~HoldsSec(c) /\ snap[c] = NoSnap
    /\ downClerks' = downClerks \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deptLock, secLock, ver, snap>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Clerks, d \in Depts : TakeDept(c, d)
    \/ \E c \in Clerks, s \in Sections : TakeSection(c, s) \/ Snapshot(c, s)
    \/ \E c \in Clerks : Commit(c) \/ CrashSilently(c) \/ ReclaimFrom(c) \/ Reboot(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
    \A c \in Clerks :
        snap[c] # NoSnap =>
            /\ secLock[snap[c].sec] = c
            /\ snap[c].base = ver[snap[c].sec]
=============================================================================
nl:
A university course-registration system lets registrar clerks edit section enrollment
records. Editing is protected by a two-level (hierarchical) lock: a clerk must first
take the coarse lock on the academic department, and only then may take the fine lock
on an individual section belonging to that department. A clerk holds at most one
department lock and at most one section lock at a time.

Once a clerk owns the fine lock on a section it takes a snapshot: it records which
section it is editing and the record version number it read. It later commits, writing
the amended roster back; the commit is only permitted if the clerk still owns the fine
lock and the version it read is still the version stored on the record. A commit bumps
the record's version number and releases both the fine and the coarse lock.

Clerks are workstations and one can crash silently at any moment, possibly while holding
both locks and while holding an unwritten snapshot. A crashed clerk can no longer take
locks, take snapshots, or commit. To keep the registrar usable, a supervisor sweep may
reclaim a crashed clerk's locks: it releases whatever department and section locks that
clerk was holding and, at the same time, discards the crashed clerk's outstanding
snapshot so that no abandoned read-modify-write can ever be applied.

Actions: a clerk takes a free department lock; a clerk that owns a department takes a
free section lock on a section of that department; a lock-holding clerk takes a version
snapshot of its section; a clerk commits its snapshot, bumping the version and releasing
both locks; a clerk crashes silently; the supervisor reclaims a crashed clerk's locks
and discards its snapshot; and a crashed clerk that has been fully reclaimed -- no locks
and no snapshot left -- reboots and rejoins as a live clerk.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every outstanding read-modify-write snapshot in the system is still
protected by its clerk's fine lock and still reads the record's current version, so no
clerk can ever write back over an update it did not see.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m3p2t5 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT TotalDoses

Controllers == {"ctA", "ctB"}

Vacant == "vacant"

VARIABLES seat, shelf, staged, dispensed, failed

vars == <<seat, shelf, staged, dispensed, failed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ seat \in Controllers \cup {Vacant}
    /\ shelf \in 0..TotalDoses
    /\ staged \subseteq Controllers
    /\ dispensed \in 0..TotalDoses
    /\ failed \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ seat = Vacant
    /\ shelf = TotalDoses
    /\ staged = {}
    /\ dispensed = 0
    /\ failed = {}

ElectLeader(c) ==
    /\ seat = Vacant
    /\ c \notin failed
    /\ seat' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, staged, dispensed, failed>>

FailController(c) ==
    /\ c \notin failed
    /\ failed' = failed \cup {c}
    /\ seat' = IF seat = c THEN Vacant ELSE seat
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, staged, dispensed>>

Rejoin(c) ==
    /\ c \in failed
    /\ c \notin staged
    /\ failed' = failed \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, shelf, staged, dispensed>>

PullDose(c) ==
    /\ seat = c
    /\ c \notin staged
    /\ shelf > 0
    /\ shelf' = shelf - 1
    /\ staged' = staged \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, dispensed, failed>>

DropToTray(c) ==
    /\ seat = c
    /\ c \in staged
    /\ staged' = staged \ {c}
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, shelf, failed>>

ReclaimStray(c) ==
    /\ seat # c
    /\ c \in staged
    /\ staged' = staged \ {c}
    /\ shelf' = shelf + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, dispensed, failed>>

AdminOverride(c) ==
    /\ seat # c
    /\ seat' = c
    /\ failed' = failed \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, staged, dispensed>>

Next ==
    \E c \in Controllers :
        \/ ElectLeader(c) \/ FailController(c) \/ Rejoin(c)
        \/ PullDose(c) \/ DropToTray(c) \/ ReclaimStray(c) \/ AdminOverride(c)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(DropToTray("ctA") \/ ReclaimStray("ctA"))
    /\ WF_vars(DropToTray("ctB") \/ ReclaimStray("ctB"))

DoseConservation == shelf + Cardinality(staged) + dispensed = TotalDoses

GrippersDrain == \A c \in Controllers : (c \in staged) ~> (c \notin staged)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    TotalDoses = 3
INVARIANT DoseConservation
PROPERTY GrippersDrain
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser is a robotic cabinet driven by a small cluster of
controller nodes. Exactly one controller acts as the dispensing leader at a time; the
others stand by and take over if the leader fails. Every physical dose in the cabinet is
in exactly one of three places: sitting on the shelf, held in a controller's staging
gripper after it has been pulled for a prescription -- a gripper is a single-slot arm and
holds at most one dose, or already dispensed to a patient.
Doses are never manufactured or destroyed by the machine.

The leader pulls a dose from the shelf into its own gripper, and later drops a held dose
into the patient tray, which counts it as dispensed. A controller that is not the current
leader has no business holding a dose, so the cabinet's reclaim arm returns any dose held
by a non-leader back to the shelf. A controller can fail at any time; if the failed
controller was the leader, the leadership seat is vacated and a standby controller is
elected in its place. A failed controller may rejoin the cluster once its gripper is
empty.

Because this is a pharmacy, a supervising pharmacist has a privileged admin override:
they may seize the dispensing seat and hand it to any controller they choose, whether or
not a leader is currently seated and whether or not that controller had previously been
marked failed.

Actions: a standby controller is elected leader when the seat is vacant; a controller
fails, vacating the seat if it held it; a failed controller with an empty gripper
rejoins; the leader pulls a dose from the shelf into its empty gripper; the leader drops a held
dose into the patient tray; the reclaim arm returns a non-leader's held dose to the
shelf; the pharmacist's admin override installs a chosen controller as leader.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of doses on the shelf, plus the doses held in controller
grippers, plus the doses already dispensed always equals the cabinet's original dose
count, so no dose is ever created or lost by any leadership change or override.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a controller has a dose in its gripper, that gripper is
eventually empty again, so every pulled dose is either dispensed to the patient or
returned to the shelf rather than being stranded in the arm.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m3p1t5 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANT StampRing

Servers == {"spoolA", "spoolB", "spoolC"}
Vacant == "vacant"
NoDraft == StampRing

VARIABLES seat, stamp, draft, failed

vars == <<seat, stamp, draft, failed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ seat \in Servers \cup {Vacant}
    /\ stamp \in 0..(StampRing - 1)
    /\ draft \in [Servers -> 0..StampRing]
    /\ failed \subseteq Servers

Init ==
    /\ seat = Vacant
    /\ stamp = 0
    /\ draft = [s \in Servers |-> NoDraft]
    /\ failed = {}

ElectStandby(s) ==
    /\ seat = Vacant
    /\ s \notin failed
    /\ seat' = s
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![s] = NoDraft]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, failed>>

StepDown(s) ==
    /\ seat = s
    /\ seat' = Vacant
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, draft, failed>>

FailServer(s) ==
    /\ s \notin failed
    /\ failed' = failed \cup {s}
    /\ seat' = IF seat = s THEN Vacant ELSE seat
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, draft>>

RejoinGroup(s) ==
    /\ s \in failed
    /\ failed' = failed \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, stamp, draft>>

TakeDraft(s) ==
    /\ seat = s
    /\ draft[s] = NoDraft
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![s] = stamp]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, stamp, failed>>

PublishDraft(s) ==
    /\ seat = s
    /\ draft[s] = stamp
    /\ stamp' = (stamp + 1) % StampRing
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![s] = NoDraft]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, failed>>

ThrowAwayDraft(s) ==
    /\ draft[s] # NoDraft
    /\ ~(seat = s /\ draft[s] = stamp)
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![s] = NoDraft]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seat, stamp, failed>>

ManagerOverride(s) ==
    /\ seat # s
    /\ seat' = s
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![s] = NoDraft]
    /\ failed' = failed \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED stamp

Next ==
    \E s \in Servers :
        \/ ElectStandby(s) \/ StepDown(s) \/ FailServer(s) \/ RejoinGroup(s)
        \/ TakeDraft(s) \/ PublishDraft(s) \/ ThrowAwayDraft(s) \/ ManagerOverride(s)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(PublishDraft("spoolA") \/ ThrowAwayDraft("spoolA"))
    /\ WF_vars(PublishDraft("spoolB") \/ ThrowAwayDraft("spoolB"))
    /\ WF_vars(PublishDraft("spoolC") \/ ThrowAwayDraft("spoolC"))

NoLostManifestUpdate ==
    \A s \in Servers : (seat = s /\ draft[s] # NoDraft) => draft[s] = stamp

DraftsAlwaysSettle ==
    \A s \in Servers : (draft[s] # NoDraft) ~> (draft[s] = NoDraft)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    StampRing = 3
INVARIANT NoLostManifestUpdate
PROPERTY DraftsAlwaysSettle
nl:
A print shop job spooler keeps one shared manifest record describing which press each
queued job is bound for. A small group of spool servers manages it, but only one of them
holds the spooling seat at a time; the others are standbys ready to take over when the
seat holder fails. The manifest carries a revision stamp, a small wrapping counter that
advances by one every time the manifest is rewritten and rolls back to zero when it runs
past its highest value.

Rewriting the manifest is a read-modify-write. The seat holder first takes a working
draft, recording the revision stamp it saw. Later it publishes the draft, which is only
allowed if it still holds the seat and the stamp it recorded is still the stamp on the
manifest; publishing advances the stamp and clears the draft. A draft that can no longer
be published -- because its holder lost the seat, or because the manifest moved on
underneath it -- is thrown away rather than applied.

A spool server may step down voluntarily, leaving the seat vacant, and a standby is then
elected into the vacant seat. Servers can also fail outright, which vacates the seat if
the failed server was holding it, and can later rejoin the group. Whenever a server takes
the seat -- by election or otherwise -- it discards any working draft it was still
carrying and starts from the manifest as it currently stands.

The shop's night manager has a privileged override: they can hand the spooling seat to
any server they name, even one that is currently marked failed and even while another
server is seated. A server installed this way also starts from a clean draft.

Actions: a standby is elected into the vacant seat; the seat holder steps down; a server
fails, vacating the seat if it held it; a failed server rejoins; the seat holder takes a
working draft of the manifest; the seat holder publishes its draft, advancing the
revision stamp; an unpublishable draft is thrown away; the night manager's override
installs a named server in the seat with a clean draft.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any working draft still held by the server that currently occupies the
spooling seat always records the manifest's current revision stamp, so no publish can
ever overwrite a manifest revision its author never read.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every working draft that a server takes is eventually gone from that
server, so no draft is left dangling forever without being either published or thrown
away.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od0m0p0t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Teams, TagRing

Rooms == {"orNorth", "orSouth"}
Nobody == "nobody"
NoRead == [rm |-> "noRoom", v |-> 0]

VARIABLES board, tag, note, phase, commissioned

vars == <<board, tag, note, phase, commissioned>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ board \in [Rooms -> Teams \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ tag \in [Rooms -> 0..(TagRing - 1)]
    /\ note \in [Teams -> [rm : Rooms \cup {"noRoom"}, v : 0..(TagRing - 1)]]
    /\ phase \in [Teams -> {"idle", "read", "operating"}]
    /\ commissioned \subseteq Rooms

Init ==
    /\ board = [r \in Rooms |-> Nobody]
    /\ tag = [r \in Rooms |-> 0]
    /\ note = [t \in Teams |-> NoRead]
    /\ phase = [t \in Teams |-> "idle"]
    /\ commissioned = Rooms

ReadBoard(t, r) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "idle"
    /\ r \in commissioned
    /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![t] = [rm |-> r, v |-> tag[r]]]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "read"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<board, tag, commissioned>>

AttemptAccepted(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "read"
    /\ LET r == note[t].rm IN
       /\ r \in commissioned
       /\ tag[r] = note[t].v
       /\ board[r] = Nobody
       /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![r] = t]
       /\ tag' = [tag EXCEPT ![r] = (@ + 1) % TagRing]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "operating"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<note, commissioned>>

AttemptRejected(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "read"
    /\ LET r == note[t].rm IN
         \/ r \notin commissioned
         \/ tag[r] # note[t].v
         \/ board[r] # Nobody
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![t] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<board, tag, commissioned>>

CaseFinished(t) ==
    /\ phase[t] = "operating"
    /\ LET r == note[t].rm IN
       /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![r] = Nobody]
       /\ tag' = [tag EXCEPT ![r] = (@ + 1) % TagRing]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
    /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![t] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED commissioned

Decommission(r) ==
    /\ r \in commissioned
    /\ board[r] = Nobody
    /\ commissioned' = commissioned \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<board, tag, note, phase>>

Recommission(r) ==
    /\ r \notin commissioned
    /\ commissioned' = commissioned \cup {r}
    /\ tag' = [tag EXCEPT ![r] = (@ + 1) % TagRing]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<board, note, phase>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Teams, r \in Rooms : ReadBoard(t, r)
    \/ \E t \in Teams : AttemptAccepted(t) \/ AttemptRejected(t) \/ CaseFinished(t)
    \/ \E r \in Rooms : Decommission(r) \/ Recommission(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OperatingIsSanctioned ==
    \A t \in Teams :
        phase[t] = "operating" =>
            /\ board[note[t].rm] = t
            /\ note[t].rm \in commissioned
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Teams = {tmRed, tmBlue}
    TagRing = 3
INVARIANT OperatingIsSanctioned
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler assigns surgical teams to operating rooms. Only the
rooms that are currently commissioned are usable, and the hospital commissions and
decommissions rooms while the scheduler is running: a room can be pulled out of service
for cleaning or maintenance, but only when nobody is booked into it, and a room that has
been out of service can be brought back.

Booking is optimistic rather than locked. Each room's board carries a revision tag, a
small wrapping counter. A team that wants a room reads the room's board in one go,
recording which room it looked at and the revision tag it saw. It then attempts to take
the room: the attempt is accepted only if the room is still commissioned, the board still
shows the team's recorded revision tag, and no other team is already written on the
board. An accepted attempt writes the team onto the room's board, advances the revision
tag, and the team scrubs in. If any of those conditions fails -- the room went out of
service, another team got there first, or the tag moved -- the attempt is rejected and
the team drops back to idle to try again from a fresh read. When a team finishes its
case it clears its name from the board, advances the revision tag, and goes idle.

Actions: an idle team reads a room's board and records the revision tag it saw; a team's
booking attempt is accepted and it scrubs in; a team's booking attempt is rejected and it
returns to idle; an operating team finishes its case and clears the board; the hospital
decommissions an unbooked room; the hospital recommissions an out-of-service room.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a team is operating, the board of the room it read names that
same team and the room is still commissioned, so no two teams can ever be operating in
one room and nobody operates in a room that is out of service.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m3p6t0 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxTerm

NoCtl == "noController"
NoCmd == [by |-> NoCtl, tm |-> 0]

VARIABLES term, dispatcher, believes, bus, crashed

vars == <<term, dispatcher, believes, bus, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ dispatcher \in Controllers \cup {NoCtl}
    /\ believes \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ bus \in [by : Controllers \cup {NoCtl}, tm : 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ dispatcher = NoCtl
    /\ believes = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ bus = NoCmd
    /\ crashed = {}

StandForElection(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ dispatcher' = c
    /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![c] = term + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, crashed>>

SyncTerm(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ believes[c] # term
    /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![c] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, dispatcher, bus, crashed>>

LatchCommand(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ dispatcher = c
    /\ believes[c] = term
    /\ bus = NoCmd
    /\ bus' = [by |-> c, tm |-> term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, dispatcher, believes, crashed>>

CarDrives ==
    /\ bus # NoCmd
    /\ bus.tm = term
    /\ bus' = NoCmd
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, dispatcher, believes, crashed>>

CarDiscardsStale ==
    /\ bus # NoCmd
    /\ bus.tm < term
    /\ bus' = NoCmd
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, dispatcher, believes, crashed>>

CrashSilently(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, dispatcher, believes, bus>>

PowerCycle(c) ==
    /\ c \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {c}
    /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![c] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, dispatcher, bus>>

Next ==
    \/ CarDrives \/ CarDiscardsStale
    \/ \E c \in Controllers :
           \/ StandForElection(c) \/ SyncTerm(c) \/ LatchCommand(c)
           \/ CrashSilently(c) \/ PowerCycle(c)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(CarDrives \/ CarDiscardsStale)

LiveCommandIsAuthorized ==
    (bus # NoCmd /\ bus.tm = term) => dispatcher = bus.by

BusAlwaysClears == (bus # NoCmd) ~> (bus = NoCmd)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {carA, carB, carC}
    MaxTerm = 2
INVARIANT LiveCommandIsAuthorized
PROPERTY BusAlwaysClears
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is driven by a group of car controllers, one of which
holds the dispatcher seat and is the only one allowed to put a movement command onto the
shared car bus. Leadership is organised in numbered terms. A controller can stand for
election at any moment; doing so raises the bank's term by one, installs that controller
as dispatcher, and leaves it believing the new term number. Followers learn the current
term number separately, by picking it up from the bank's heartbeat.

The car bus latches at most one command at a time, and the latched command carries the
term of the controller that issued it. A controller may issue a command only when it
holds the dispatcher seat and its own believed term matches the bank's current term. The
car itself carries out a latched command when the command's term is still the current
term; if an election has moved the bank on, the car discards the stale command instead of
driving on it. Either way the bus ends up empty again.

A controller can crash silently at any time. Nothing announces the failure: the crashed
controller simply stops standing for election, stops syncing the term, and stops issuing
commands, and it may still be sitting in the dispatcher seat. Failover happens when
another controller stands for election on a higher term, which deposes whoever was
seated. A crashed controller can be power-cycled and rejoin the bank, coming back with no
memory of the term it used to believe.

Actions: a live controller stands for election, raising the term and taking the seat; a
live controller syncs its believed term from the heartbeat; the seated dispatcher latches
a command onto the car bus; the car carries out a current-term command and clears the
bus; the car discards a stale command and clears the bus; a controller crashes silently;
a crashed controller is power-cycled and rejoins with a reset belief.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any command latched on the car bus that still carries the bank's current
term was issued by the controller that currently holds the dispatcher seat, so no
unseated or deposed controller can ever have a live command driving the cars.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a command is latched on the car bus, the bus eventually
becomes empty again, so no command sits latched forever undriven and undiscarded.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m3p2t4 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Coordinators, TotalUnits, MinShelves, MaxShelves

Empty == "emptySeat"

VARIABLES fridge, carrying, wards, seat, shelfCap

vars == <<fridge, carrying, wards, seat, shelfCap>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ fridge \in 0..TotalUnits
    /\ carrying \subseteq Coordinators
    /\ wards \in 0..TotalUnits
    /\ seat \in Coordinators \cup {Empty}
    /\ shelfCap \in MinShelves..MaxShelves

Init ==
    /\ fridge = TotalUnits
    /\ carrying = {}
    /\ wards = 0
    /\ seat = Empty
    /\ shelfCap = MaxShelves

ElectIntoSeat(c) ==
    /\ seat = Empty
    /\ seat' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, carrying, wards, shelfCap>>

SeatFailsOver ==
    /\ seat # Empty
    /\ seat' = Empty
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridge, carrying, wards, shelfCap>>

PullFromFridge(c) ==
    /\ seat = c
    /\ c \notin carrying
    /\ fridge > 0
    /\ fridge' = fridge - 1
    /\ carrying' = carrying \cup {c}

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker follows a fixed pool of blood units around a hospital.
Every unit is at any moment in exactly one of three places: chilled in the bank's fridge,
riding in a courier coordinator's insulated carrier, or delivered up on a ward. A carrier
is a single-unit cooler, so a coordinator either has one unit with them or none.

The coordinators run as a small cluster with one of them holding the dispatch seat. Only
the coordinator holding the seat is allowed to pull a unit out of the fridge into its
carrier. The seat can fail over at any time: the seated coordinator drops the seat and a
different coordinator is later elected into the empty seat. A coordinator that loses the
seat while carrying a unit keeps that unit in its carrier and may still finish the trip:
it can hand the unit up to a ward, or bring it back and re-chill it in the fridge. Units
that a ward does not use are returned to the fridge as well.

The fridge's shelf capacity is not fixed. Shelves are pulled for defrosting and put back
during the day, so the number of units the fridge can chill goes up and down while the
tracker is running. A shelf may only be pulled while the fridge still has slack -- the
units already chilled must fit in the reduced space -- and a unit may only be re-chilled
or returned if the fridge has room for it under the capacity in force at that moment.

Actions: a coordinator is elected into the empty dispatch seat; the seated coordinator
drops the seat on failure; the seated coordinator pulls a unit from the fridge into its
carrier; a carrying coordinator hands its unit up to a ward; a carrying coordinator
re-chills its unit in the fridge; a ward returns an unused unit to the fridge; a shelf is
pulled, reducing fridge capacity; a shelf is put back, raising fridge capacity.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of units chilled in the fridge, plus the units riding in
coordinators' carriers, plus the units delivered to wards always equals the bank's total
unit pool, so no seat failover, re-chill, or capacity change ever creates or loses a unit.

nl:
A container-ship crane yard is worked by two completely independent terminal-management
instances, one belonging to each operator sharing the quay. They have no shared scheduler
and no shared plan; they simply both drive cranes over the same physical pool of
containers, which sit either in one of the two stacking bays, in a crane's spreader while
it is in the air, or already stowed on the ship.

Because the two instances are independent, they coordinate only through one optimistic
lock: a move register on the quay that ticks forward every time a container leaves a bay.
An instance that wants to lift first reads the move register and remembers the value it
saw. It may then lift a container out of a bay only if the register still reads exactly
what it remembered; the lift takes the container out of the bay into the instance's
spreader and ticks the register. If the register has moved on since the read -- because
the other instance lifted in between -- the instance abandons its stale read and starts
over with a fresh one. A crane's spreader carries at most one container.

A container in a spreader is eventually put down: it is either stowed on the ship or set
back down in one of the two bays. Independently of the cranes, the quay gantry can take a
container back off the ship and set it down in a bay.

Actions: an instance reads the move register; an instance with a matching read lifts a
container out of a bay and ticks the register; an instance discards a read the register
has moved past and starts over; an instance stows the container in its spreader on the
ship; an instance sets the container in its spreader back down in a bay; the gantry takes
a container off the ship and sets it down in a bay.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The containers in the north bay, the containers in the south bay, the
containers hanging in the two instances' spreaders, and the containers stowed on the ship
always add up to the quay's total container pool, so no lift, stow, or stale-read retry
ever duplicates or drops a container.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Any container hanging in an instance's spreader is eventually put
down, so no crane is left holding a container in the air forever.

    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, held, settled, replay, windowOpen>>

    Workers = {wkA, wkB}

nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch moves payment instructions out to the settlement rail.
Actually settling an instruction is irreversible: once the money has left, it cannot be
recalled, so an instruction must never settle twice.

Instructions arrive from the gateway and wait to be admitted into a bounded work queue.
The queue holds only a fixed number of instructions, and that bound is real backpressure:
while the queue is full nothing new is admitted, and even an instruction a settlement
worker wants to hand back has to wait for room. Admission also only happens while the
settlement window is open; the window is opened and closed through the day.

Settlement workers pull instructions out of the queue in whatever order they like, since
the rail gives no ordering guarantee. A worker holds at most one instruction at a time. It
either settles it, which is the irreversible step, or hands it back into the queue if room
allows.

The gateway keeps a replay buffer of everything it has forwarded, because instructions can
arrive at the rail out of order and the gateway may need to re-emit one that appears to
have been lost. A re-emission puts the instruction back into the queue, but only when the
instruction is genuinely nowhere in the system: not already queued, not held by a worker,
and above all not already settled. Once the gateway learns an instruction has settled it
purges it from the replay buffer entirely.

Actions: the gateway admits a waiting instruction into the queue while the window is open
and the queue has room; a worker pulls an instruction out of the queue; a worker settles
the instruction it holds; a worker hands its unsettled instruction back into the queue if
there is room; the gateway re-emits a genuinely absent instruction from its replay buffer;
the gateway purges a settled instruction from its replay buffer; the settlement window
opens; the settlement window closes.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No instruction that has already settled is ever sitting in the work queue
or held by a settlement worker, so nothing that has settled can be picked up and settled a
second time.

nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper keeps its hoistway doors locked except while a
maintenance technician is working a car. Authority to unlock a door comes from a single
compare-and-swap interlock register, which names the technician currently holding
authority and carries a stamp that ticks every time authority changes hands.

A technician who wants authority first reads the register's stamp, then attempts the
compare-and-swap: it succeeds only if the register is still unheld and its stamp is still
the value the technician read, and it installs the technician as holder with a ticked
stamp. If the register has been taken or its stamp has moved, the attempt misses and the
technician goes back to reading. While a technician holds the register it may unlock the
hoistway door of any car; the door records which technician unlocked it. A car's own
controller relocks an unlocked door once the work at that car is over.

A technician may hand the register back, but only after every door it unlocked has been
relocked, at which point the stamp ticks again.

A technician can crash silently: it simply stops reading, stops attempting the swap,
stops unlocking, and never hands the register back, possibly while still holding it and
possibly with doors still unlocked in its name. The bank's watchdog handles this: it
fences a crashed holder by relocking every door standing open in that technician's name
and releasing the register with a ticked stamp, in one step. A crashed technician can be
restarted and resumes with no remembered stamp.

Actions: a technician reads the register's stamp; a technician's compare-and-swap
succeeds and installs it as holder; a technician's compare-and-swap misses and it starts
over; the holding technician unlocks a car's hoistway door; a car controller relocks an
unlocked door; the holder hands back the register once none of its doors are open; a
technician crashes silently; the watchdog fences a crashed holder, relocking its doors
and releasing the register; a crashed technician restarts.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any hoistway door standing unlocked was unlocked by the technician the
interlock register currently names as holder, so no door is ever left open in the name of
a technician that has been fenced, has handed the register back, or never held it.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every hoistway door that is unlocked eventually becomes locked again,
so no car is left standing open forever.

nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has several wash bays fed by one shared high-pressure pump. The
pump is the critical resource: it has only enough head for a single bay at a time, so
exactly one crew may be spraying out of it.

Access is taken through two levels of lock, coarse before fine. A crew first takes the
line lock, which covers the whole conveyor, and only while holding the line lock may it
take the lock on a particular bay. The moment a crew has its bay lock it hands the line
lock straight back, so the coarse lock is only ever held long enough to pick a bay and
other crews keep moving. A crew holding a bay may then start spraying, which is allowed
only when the pump is idle, and it claims the pump for itself. It stops spraying when the
car is done, releasing the pump. A crew may give up its bay only once it is no longer
spraying, at which point the bay lock goes back to free.

A wash crew can crash silently: its console simply stops, and it may be stopped mid-spray
while holding the pump, a bay, or the line lock, with nothing announcing the failure. The
line supervisor deals with this by sweeping the crashed crew: in one step the supervisor
drops the pump if the crashed crew had it, frees the line lock and any bay lock standing
in that crew's name, and puts the crew back to idle. A crashed crew that has been swept
back to idle can be brought back online.

Actions: an idle crew takes the free line lock; a crew holding the line lock takes a free
bay lock and hands the line lock back; a crew holding a bay starts spraying and claims the
idle pump; a spraying crew stops and releases the pump; a non-spraying crew gives up its
bay lock and goes idle; a crew crashes silently; the supervisor sweeps a crashed crew,
dropping its pump and freeing its locks; a swept crew is brought back online.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any crew that is spraying holds the pump itself and still holds a bay
lock, so the pump is never drawn by two crews at once and never by a crew that has no bay.

RestartTech(t) ==
    /\ t \in crashed
    /\ bench[t] = NoReq
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inbox, intake, bench, completed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Requests : AdmitRequest(r)
    \/ \E t \in Techs :
           \/ TakeHeadOntoBench(t) \/ CompleteCrossmatch(t)
           \/ CrashSilently(t) \/ SupervisorRequeues(t) \/ RestartTech(t)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(CompleteCrossmatch("benchOne") \/ SupervisorRequeues("benchOne"))
    /\ WF_vars(CompleteCrossmatch("benchTwo") \/ SupervisorRequeues("benchTwo"))

BenchesClearOut ==
    \A t \in Techs : (bench[t] # NoReq) ~> (bench[t] = NoReq)

cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Licence = 2
INVARIANT LicenceNeverBreached
PROPERTY BenchesClearOut
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker feeds cross-match requests to the bench technicians. The
bank is licensed for a fixed number of open cross-matches at once, and that licence is the
capacity the tracker must never breach.

Requests arrive in an inbox and are admitted, in order, onto a bounded intake queue. A
request that has been admitted occupies one of the licensed slots, and it keeps occupying
that slot the whole time it is in the system: while it waits in the queue and also while a
technician has it on the bench. Admission is therefore refused -- this is the
backpressure -- whenever the queue length plus the number of requests currently on
benches has reached the licence. A technician takes the request at the head of the queue
onto its bench, works it, and completes the cross-match, which is when the slot is finally
given back.

A bench technician can crash silently, mid-request, with nothing announcing it. The
request on that technician's bench is not lost: the shift supervisor puts it back onto the
tail of the intake queue, which moves the slot from the bench back to the queue without
ever changing how many slots are in use. A crashed technician whose bench has been cleared
can be restarted.

Actions: the tracker admits an inbox request onto the tail of the intake queue when the
licence has room; a technician takes the head request of the queue onto its bench; a
technician completes the cross-match on its bench and gives the slot back; a technician
crashes silently; the supervisor puts a crashed technician's bench request back onto the
tail of the queue; a crashed technician with an empty bench is restarted.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of requests waiting on the intake queue plus the number of
technicians with a request on the bench never exceeds the bank's licensed number of open
cross-matches.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every request that lands on a technician's bench eventually leaves that
bench, either completed or put back on the queue, so nothing sits on a bench forever.

CONSTANTS Handhelds, MaxStock, LeaseLife

Machines == {"vendLobby", "vendGarage"}
NoHH == "noHandheld"
NoMachine == "noMachine"
NoDraft == [mc |-> NoMachine, saw |-> 0]

VARIABLES stock, leaseOwner, countdown, draft, dead

vars == <<stock, leaseOwner, countdown, draft, dead>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ stock \in [Machines -> 0..MaxStock]
    /\ leaseOwner \in [Machines -> Handhelds \cup {NoHH}]
    /\ countdown \in [Machines -> 0..LeaseLife]
    /\ draft \in [Handhelds -> [mc : Machines \cup {NoMachine}, saw : 0..MaxStock]]
    /\ dead \subseteq Handhelds

Init ==
    /\ stock = [m \in Machines |-> 1]
    /\ leaseOwner = [m \in Machines |-> NoHH]
    /\ countdown = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ draft = [h \in Handhelds |-> NoDraft]
    /\ dead = {}

GrantLease(h, m) ==
    /\ h \notin dead
    /\ leaseOwner[m] = NoHH
    /\ leaseOwner' = [leaseOwner EXCEPT ![m] = h]
    /\ countdown' = [countdown EXCEPT ![m] = LeaseLife]
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![h] = NoDraft]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, dead>>

ReadIntoDraft(h, m) ==
    /\ h \notin dead
    /\ leaseOwner[m] = h
    /\ draft[h] = NoDraft
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![h] = [mc |-> m, saw |-> stock[m]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, leaseOwner, countdown, dead>>

WriteAmendment(h, n) ==
    /\ h \notin dead
    /\ draft[h] # NoDraft
    /\ LET m == draft[h].mc IN
       /\ leaseOwner[m] = h
       /\ countdown[m] > 0
       /\ draft[h].saw = stock[m]
       /\ n \in {stock[m] - 1, stock[m] + 1}
       /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![m] = n]
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![h] = NoDraft]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, countdown, dead>>

AbandonDraft(h) ==
    /\ draft[h] # NoDraft
    /\ leaseOwner[draft[h].mc] # h
    /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![h] = NoDraft]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, leaseOwner, countdown, dead>>

CountdownTicks(m) ==
    /\ countdown[m] > 0
    /\ countdown' = [countdown EXCEPT ![m] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, leaseOwner, draft, dead>>

ReclaimLapsed(m) ==
    /\ countdown[m] = 0
    /\ leaseOwner[m] # NoHH
    /\ leaseOwner' = [leaseOwner EXCEPT ![m] = NoHH]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, countdown, draft, dead>>

GiveBackLease(h, m) ==
    /\ h \notin dead
    /\ leaseOwner[m] = h
    /\ draft[h].mc # m
    /\ leaseOwner' = [leaseOwner EXCEPT ![m] = NoHH]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, countdown, draft, dead>>

CrashSilently(h) ==
    /\ h \notin dead
    /\ dead' = dead \cup {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, leaseOwner, countdown, draft>>

    /\ h \in dead
    /\ draft[h] = NoDraft
    /\ \A m \in Machines : leaseOwner[m] # h
    /\ dead' = dead \ {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, leaseOwner, countdown, draft>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Handhelds, m \in Machines :
           GrantLease(h, m) \/ ReadIntoDraft(h, m) \/ GiveBackLease(h, m)
    \/ \E h \in Handhelds, n \in 0..MaxStock : WriteAmendment(h, n)
    \/ \E h \in Handhelds : AbandonDraft(h) \/ CrashSilently(h) \/ ReImage(h)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : CountdownTicks(m) \/ ReclaimLapsed(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

        (draft[h] # NoDraft /\ leaseOwner[draft[h].mc] = h) => draft[h].saw = stock[draft[h].mc]

cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Handhelds = {hhOne, hhTwo}
    MaxStock = 2
    LeaseLife = 1
INVARIANT LeasedDraftIsCurrent
nl:
A vending machine network keeps one stock record per machine, giving the counted number of
units loaded in it. Field service handhelds amend those records, and to stop two handhelds
writing over each other the network hands out leases: a handheld takes the lease on a
machine, and only the current lease holder may amend that machine's record.

Leases are not held forever. Each lease carries a countdown; the countdown ticks down on
its own, and when it reaches the end the network takes the lease back and the machine is
free for anyone to lease again. A handheld may also give a lease back voluntarily, as long
as it is not in the middle of an amendment on that machine.

Amending is a read-modify-write. Holding a lease, the handheld reads the machine's record
and keeps that reading as a working draft; later it writes the amendment, moving the
count one unit up or one unit down, and the write is accepted only if the handheld still
holds the lease, the lease has not run out, and the count it read is still the count in
the record. When a handheld is granted a lease on a machine it always starts from a fresh
reading, so any draft it was still carrying is dropped at that moment. A draft whose lease
has gone to somebody else, or lapsed, is abandoned rather than written.

A handheld can crash silently in the field: it stops reading, stops writing, and never
gives its lease back. Nothing announces this; the lease countdown simply runs out and the
network reclaims the machine. A crashed handheld that holds no lease and carries no draft
can be re-imaged and put back into service.

Actions: a handheld is granted the free lease on a machine and starts from a fresh
reading; a lease holder reads a machine's record into a working draft; a lease holder
writes an amendment moving the count one unit up or down; a handheld abandons a draft whose lease it no longer holds; a lease countdown ticks
down; a lapsed lease is reclaimed by the network; a handheld gives back a lease it is not
amending; a handheld crashes silently; a crashed, lease-free handheld is re-imaged.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any working draft whose handheld still holds the lease on the machine it
read records that machine's current count, so no amendment can ever be written on top of a
count its author never saw.

cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OpenProposalIsUnetched
PROPERTY ProposalsAlwaysClose
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line offers an acid-etch clearcoat step. Etching a car is
irreversible: the coat cannot be stripped back off, so a given car must never be etched
twice.

The line will not etch on one controller's say-so. A proposal to etch a particular car is
opened on the line bus, and the three bay controllers vote on it. A controller votes at
most once on the proposal that is currently open, and the etch head only fires once a
strict majority of the controllers have voted for the open proposal. Firing the head
etches that car and closes the proposal, clearing the tally so that the next proposal
starts from no votes. A proposal may only be opened for a car that has not been etched
already, and only when no other proposal is open.

Controllers on this line are slow, never failed. A controller can drop into a slow spell
where its vote does not get onto the bus, and it comes out of that spell again on its own;
it never stops answering permanently, so a controller in a slow spell is always going to
be back.

Actions: a proposal to etch an un-etched car is opened while the bus is free; a
controller that is not in a slow spell casts its vote for the open proposal; the etch head
fires once a strict majority has voted, etching the car and closing the proposal; a
controller drops into a slow spell; a controller comes out of a slow spell.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The car named by an open etch proposal has never been etched, so the etch
head can never fire twice on the same car.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every etch proposal that is opened is eventually closed, so the line
bus never sits blocked on a proposal that stays open forever.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m8p1t3 -------------------------

Crews == {"crewNorth", "crewSouth"}
Bays == {"bayOne", "bayTwo"}

FreeLock == "freeLock"
NoBay == "noBay"
ClearBoard == [bay |-> NoBay, copy |-> {}]

VARIABLES lineLock, bayLock, ledger, clipboard, slowSpell

vars == <<lineLock, bayLock, ledger, clipboard, slowSpell>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ lineLock \in Crews \cup {FreeLock}
    /\ bayLock \in [Bays -> Crews \cup {FreeLock}]
    /\ ledger \in [Bays -> SUBSET Chemicals]
    /\ clipboard \in [Crews -> [bay : Bays \cup {NoBay}, copy : SUBSET Chemicals]]
    /\ slowSpell \subseteq Crews

Init ==
    /\ lineLock = FreeLock
    /\ bayLock = [b \in Bays |-> FreeLock]
    /\ ledger = [b \in Bays |-> {}]
    /\ clipboard = [k \in Crews |-> ClearBoard]
    /\ slowSpell = {}

TakeLineLock(k) ==
    /\ k \notin slowSpell
    /\ lineLock = FreeLock
    /\ \A b \in Bays : bayLock[b] # k
    /\ lineLock' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bayLock, ledger, clipboard, slowSpell>>

TakeBayHandBackLine(k, b) ==
    /\ k \notin slowSpell
    /\ lineLock = k
    /\ bayLock[b] = FreeLock
    /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![b] = k]
    /\ lineLock' = FreeLock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, clipboard, slowSpell>>

CopyToClipboard(k, b) ==

    /\ bayLock[b] = k
    /\ clipboard[k] = ClearBoard
    /\ clipboard' = [clipboard EXCEPT ![k] = [bay |-> b, copy |-> ledger[b]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, bayLock, ledger, slowSpell>>

WriteBack(k, ch) ==
    /\ k \notin slowSpell
    /\ clipboard[k] # ClearBoard
    /\ bayLock[clipboard[k].bay] = k
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![clipboard[k].bay] = clipboard[k].copy \cup {ch}]
    /\ clipboard' = [clipboard EXCEPT ![k] = ClearBoard]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, bayLock, slowSpell>>

GiveUpBay(k, b) ==
    /\ k \notin slowSpell
    /\ bayLock[b] = k
    /\ clipboard[k] = ClearBoard
    /\ bayLock' = [bayLock EXCEPT ![b] = FreeLock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, ledger, clipboard, slowSpell>>

FallSlow(k) ==
    /\ k \notin slowSpell
    /\ slowSpell' = slowSpell \cup {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, bayLock, ledger, clipboard>>

ComeRound(k) ==
    /\ k \in slowSpell
    /\ slowSpell' = slowSpell \ {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineLock, bayLock, ledger, clipboard>>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Crews : TakeLineLock(k) \/ FallSlow(k) \/ ComeRound(k)
    \/ \E k \in Crews, b \in Bays :
           TakeBayHandBackLine(k, b) \/ CopyToClipboard(k, b) \/ GiveUpBay(k, b)
    \/ \E k \in Crews, ch \in Chemicals : WriteBack(k, ch)

    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ SF_vars(\E ch \in Chemicals : WriteBack("crewNorth", ch))
    /\ SF_vars(\E ch \in Chemicals : WriteBack("crewSouth", ch))
    /\ WF_vars(ComeRound("crewNorth"))
    /\ WF_vars(ComeRound("crewSouth"))

        clipboard[k] # ClearBoard => clipboard[k].copy = ledger[clipboard[k].bay]

ClipboardsAlwaysClear ==

cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ClipboardMatchesLedger
PROPERTY ClipboardsAlwaysClear
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line keeps a chemical ledger for each bay listing which chemicals are
currently dosed into that bay's feed. Crews amend those ledgers, and the amendment is a
read-modify-write: a crew copies the bay's ledger into its clipboard, then writes the
copied list back with one more chemical added.

Two levels of lock protect this, coarse before fine. A crew first takes the line lock,
which covers the whole conveyor, and only while holding it may it take the lock on a
particular bay's ledger. As soon as the bay lock is in hand the line lock goes straight
back, so the coarse lock is held only long enough to pick a bay. A crew may copy a
ledger onto its clipboard only while holding that bay's lock, and it writes its clipboard
back to the same bay while still holding the lock. A crew gives up a bay lock only once
its clipboard is clear.

Crews here are slow, never failed. A crew can fall into a slow spell in which it does
nothing at all -- it does not take locks, does not copy, does not write back, and does not
release anything -- and it comes out of the spell on its own. Because a slow crew is
indistinguishable from a stopped one and is known never to have stopped, nothing ever
takes a lock away from a crew: there is no timeout and no sweep, and a slow crew that
holds a bay lock keeps it until it comes round and releases it itself.

Actions: an idle crew takes the free line lock; a crew holding the line lock takes a free
bay lock and hands the line lock back; a crew holding a bay lock copies that bay's ledger
onto its clipboard; a crew writes its clipboard back to the bay it copied, adding a
chemical; a crew with a clear clipboard gives up its bay lock; a crew falls into a slow
spell; a crew comes out of a slow spell.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any clipboard a crew is carrying holds exactly the chemical list that its
bay's ledger currently shows, so a crew can never write back a list that another crew's
amendment has already moved past.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every clipboard a crew fills is eventually cleared again, so no crew is
left carrying an unwritten copy of a ledger forever.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANT TotalShares

Desks == {"deskA", "deskB", "deskC"}
Instances == {"instOne", "instTwo"}
NextDesk == [deskA |-> "deskB", deskB |-> "deskC", deskC |-> "deskA"]
InstanceOf == [deskA |-> "instOne", deskB |-> "instOne", deskC |-> "instTwo"]

VARIABLES token, pool, pad, print

vars == <<token, pool, pad, print>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Desks
    /\ pool \in 0..TotalShares
    /\ pad \in [Desks -> 0..TotalShares]
    /\ print \in [Instances -> 0..TotalShares]

Init ==
    /\ token = "deskA"
    /\ pool = TotalShares
    /\ pad = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
    /\ print = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

HandOnToken ==
    /\ pad[token] = 0
    /\ token' = NextDesk[token]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, pad, print>>

PullFromPool ==
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ pad' = [pad EXCEPT ![token] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, print>>

CrossIntoPrint(d) ==
    /\ pad[d] > 0
    /\ pad' = [pad EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1]
    /\ print' = [print EXCEPT ![InstanceOf[d]] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, pool>>

ReturnToPool(d) ==
    /\ pad[d] > 0
    /\ pad' = [pad EXCEPT ![d] = @ - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, print>>

CancelPrinted(i) ==
    /\ print[i] > 0
    /\ print' = [print EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, pad>>

Next ==
    \/ HandOnToken \/ PullFromPool
    \/ \E d \in Desks : CrossIntoPrint(d) \/ ReturnToPool(d)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : CancelPrinted(i)

    pool + pad["deskA"] + pad["deskB"] + pad["deskC"]
        + print["instOne"] + print["instTwo"] = TotalShares
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    TotalShares = 3
INVARIANT SharesAreConserved
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction is run by two completely independent matching instances
that happen to share one pool of an issue's shares. The instances have no common
scheduler and no shared book; each keeps its own opening print tally, and the only thing
that coordinates them is a token ring.

Three trading desks sit on the ring, and exactly one of them holds the ring token at any
moment. The token is what grants exclusive access to the shared pool: only the desk
holding the token may pull shares out of the pool onto its own pad. A desk hands the
token on to the next desk in ring order, but only once its own pad is empty, so a desk
never carries pulled shares across a handoff.

Shares on a desk's pad go one of two ways. They can be crossed into the opening print of
whichever instance that desk belongs to, or they can be put straight back into the shared
pool. An opening print that has already been struck can still be cancelled before the
open, which sends those shares back into the shared pool as well.

Actions: the token holder hands the token to the next desk on the ring once its pad is
empty; the token holder pulls a share out of the shared pool onto its pad; a desk crosses
a share from its pad into its own instance's opening print; a desk puts a share from its
pad back into the shared pool; an instance cancels a share from its opening print and
returns it to the shared pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shares sitting in the shared pool, plus the shares on the three
desks' pads, plus the shares crossed into the two instances' opening prints always add up
to the issue's total share count, so no pull, cross, return, or cancellation ever creates
or destroys a share.

vars == <<term, leader, orderBus, incisionLog, slowSpell>>

Logged(k) == \E i \in 1..Len(incisionLog) : incisionLog[i] = k

    /\ orderBus \in [patient : Cases \cup {NoCase}, tm : 0..MaxTerm]

    /\ leader = NoCase
    /\ orderBus = NoOrder

    /\ slowSpell = {}

StandForElection(c) ==
    /\ c \notin slowSpell
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1

RaiseOrder(c, k) ==

    /\ orderBus = NoOrder
    /\ ~Logged(k)

    /\ orderBus.tm = term
    /\ ~Logged(orderBus.patient)
    /\ incisionLog' = Append(incisionLog, orderBus.patient)
    /\ orderBus' = NoOrder

    /\ \/ orderBus.tm # term
       \/ Logged(orderBus.patient)

    /\ WF_vars(TheatreActs \/ TheatreRejects)

        incisionLog[i] = incisionLog[j] => i = j

cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Coordinators = {coordOne, coordTwo}
    MaxTerm = 2
INVARIANT NoCaseOpenedTwice
PROPERTY BusAlwaysFrees
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler decides when a booked case may be opened. Making the
first incision is irreversible -- once a patient is open, that case has been started and
cannot be un-started -- so a case must never be started twice.

Scheduling coordinators run in numbered terms. A coordinator can stand for election at any
time, which raises the term by one and makes that coordinator the scheduling leader. Only
the current leader puts an incision order onto the theatre bus, and only one order sits on
the bus at a time. An order names the case and carries the term of the leader that issued
it, and a leader will only raise an order for a case that is not already in the theatre's
incision log.

The theatre itself is the last check. It acts on an order only if the order's term is
still the current term and the case is still absent from the incision log; acting appends
that case to the log, which is the irreversible step, and clears the bus. Any other order
-- one carrying a term the bank of theatres has moved past, or naming a case already in
the log -- is rejected off the bus without being acted on.

Coordinators are slow, never failed. A coordinator can fall into a slow spell where it
neither stands for election nor raises orders, and it comes out of the spell by itself.
Because it never truly stops, a coordinator that was deposed while slow is still alive
and may still be holding an order it raised in an older term; nothing fences it off
except the theatre's term check.

Actions: a coordinator that is not slow stands for election, raising the term and taking
the lead; the leader raises an incision order for a case absent from the log; the theatre
acts on a current-term order for an unlogged case, appending it to the incision log; the
theatre rejects any other order off the bus; a coordinator falls into a slow spell; a
coordinator comes out of a slow spell.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No case appears more than once in the theatre's incision log, so no
patient is ever opened twice.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every incision order that reaches the theatre bus eventually leaves it,
so the bus never stays blocked by an order that is neither acted on nor rejected.

Stations == 1..RingSize
Instances == {"dayShop", "nightShop"}
NoStation == 0
InstanceOf == [s \in Stations |-> IF s * 2 <= RingSize THEN "dayShop" ELSE "nightShop"]

VARIABLES token, burning, asked, blanks, finishedPlates

vars == <<token, burning, asked, blanks, finishedPlates>>

    /\ token \in Stations
    /\ burning \in Stations \cup {NoStation}
    /\ asked \subseteq Stations
    /\ blanks \in 0..MaxStock
    /\ finishedPlates \in [Instances -> 0..MaxPlates]

Init ==
    /\ token = 1
    /\ burning = NoStation
    /\ asked = {}
    /\ blanks = MaxStock
    /\ finishedPlates = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

AskForSetter(s) ==
    /\ s \notin asked
    /\ asked' = asked \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, burning, blanks, finishedPlates>>

StartBurn(s) ==
    /\ token = s
    /\ s \in asked
    /\ burning = NoStation
    /\ blanks > 0
    /\ burning' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, asked, blanks, finishedPlates>>

FinishBurn(s) ==
    /\ burning = s
    /\ finishedPlates[InstanceOf[s]] < MaxPlates
    /\ blanks' = blanks - 1
    /\ finishedPlates' = [finishedPlates EXCEPT ![InstanceOf[s]] = @ + 1]
    /\ burning' = NoStation
    /\ asked' = asked \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED token

    /\ burning = NoStation
    /\ token' = (token % RingSize) + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<burning, asked, blanks, finishedPlates>>

    /\ blanks < MaxStock
    /\ blanks' = blanks + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, burning, asked, finishedPlates>>

ShipPlates(i) ==
    /\ finishedPlates[i] > 0
    /\ finishedPlates' = [finishedPlates EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, burning, asked, blanks>>

    \/ \E s \in Stations : AskForSetter(s) \/ StartBurn(s) \/ FinishBurn(s)

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    MaxStock = 2
    MaxPlates = 2
INVARIANT SetterUserHoldsToken
nl:
A print shop job spooler is run by two independent instances -- the shop's day system and
its overnight system -- that share one physical plate room. Neither knows anything about
the other's schedule. What they share is the imagesetter, which is the critical resource:
it can burn only one plate at a time, and the two instances' stations must never both be
on it. They also draw plate blanks from one common stock.

Three stations sit in a numbered ring, and a ring token passes around them in order. A
station may put a job on the imagesetter only when it is holding the token, only when it
has asked for the setter, and only when the setter is free and there is a blank left in
the shared stock. Burning finishes by taking a blank out of the shared stock and adding a
finished plate to whichever instance the station belongs to.

The token only moves while the imagesetter is free. A station that is mid-burn keeps the
token until the burn is done, so the token never leaves a station that is using the
setter. Plate blanks are replenished into the shared stock as deliveries arrive.

Actions: a station asks for the imagesetter; the token-holding station that has asked
starts a burn on the free setter while a blank is in stock; a station finishes its burn,
consuming a blank and crediting a finished plate to its instance; the token passes to the
next station in ring order while the setter is free; the plate room is replenished with a
blank.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any station that is burning on the imagesetter is the station currently
holding the ring token, so two stations can never be on the setter at once.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m7p2t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS TotalStrips, RegRing

Controllers == {"ctlNorth", "ctlSouth"}
Runways == {"rwyLeft", "rwyRight"}
NoRead == RegRing

VARIABLES rack, posted, inHand, allocReg, remembered, openRunways

vars == <<rack, posted, inHand, allocReg, remembered, openRunways>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ rack \in 0..TotalStrips
    /\ posted \in [Runways -> 0..TotalStrips]
    /\ inHand \subseteq Controllers
    /\ allocReg \in 0..(RegRing - 1)
    /\ remembered \in [Controllers -> 0..RegRing]
    /\ openRunways \subseteq Runways

Init ==
    /\ rack = TotalStrips
    /\ posted = [r \in Runways |-> 0]
    /\ inHand = {}
    /\ allocReg = 0
    /\ remembered = [c \in Controllers |-> NoRead]
    /\ openRunways = Runways

ReadRegister(c) ==
    /\ remembered[c] = NoRead
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![c] = allocReg]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rack, posted, inHand, allocReg, openRunways>>

PullStrip(c) ==
    /\ remembered[c] = allocReg
    /\ c \notin inHand
    /\ rack > 0
    /\ rack' = rack - 1
    /\ inHand' = inHand \cup {c}
    /\ allocReg' = (allocReg + 1) % RegRing
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![c] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<posted, openRunways>>

DropStaleRead(c) ==
    /\ remembered[c] # NoRead
    /\ remembered[c] # allocReg
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![c] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rack, posted, inHand, allocReg, openRunways>>

PostAtRunway(c, r) ==
    /\ c \in inHand
    /\ r \in openRunways
    /\ inHand' = inHand \ {c}
    /\ posted' = [posted EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rack, allocReg, remembered, openRunways>>

RackAgain(c) ==
    /\ c \in inHand
    /\ inHand' = inHand \ {c}
    /\ rack' = rack + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<posted, allocReg, remembered, openRunways>>

MovementComplete(r) ==
    /\ posted[r] > 0
    /\ posted' = [posted EXCEPT ![r] = @ - 1]
    /\ rack' = rack + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inHand, allocReg, remembered, openRunways>>

CloseRunway(r) ==
    /\ r \in openRunways
    /\ posted[r] = 0
    /\ openRunways' = openRunways \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rack, posted, inHand, allocReg, remembered>>

ReopenRunway(r) ==
    /\ r \notin openRunways
    /\ openRunways' = openRunways \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rack, posted, inHand, allocReg, remembered>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : ReadRegister(c) \/ PullStrip(c) \/ DropStaleRead(c) \/ RackAgain(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways : PostAtRunway(c, r)
    \/ \E r \in Runways : MovementComplete(r) \/ CloseRunway(r) \/ ReopenRunway(r)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(RackAgain("ctlNorth"))
    /\ WF_vars(RackAgain("ctlSouth"))

StripsAreConserved ==
    rack + posted["rwyLeft"] + posted["rwyRight"] + Cardinality(inHand) = TotalStrips

HandsEmptyAgain ==

cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    TotalStrips = 3
    RegRing = 3
INVARIANT StripsAreConserved
PROPERTY HandsEmptyAgain
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator works with a fixed set of physical progress strips. Every
strip is at any moment in exactly one of three places: racked in the strip bay, in a
controller's hand, or posted at one of the runways. Strips are never printed and never
shredded during a shift, so the count of them cannot change.

Controllers take strips out of the rack through one compare-and-swap allocation register.
A controller reads the register, remembering the value it saw, and may then pull a strip
out of the rack only if the register still reads exactly what it remembered; the pull
ticks the register. A read the register has already moved past is discarded and the
controller reads again. A controller holds at most one strip.

A strip in hand is either posted at a runway or racked again. Posting is only allowed at
a runway that is currently open. A strip posted at a runway comes back to the rack when
that runway's movement is complete.

Runway capacity changes through the shift: runways are closed for sweeping, inspection or
weather and are reopened afterwards. A runway may only be closed when nothing is posted at
it, so closing never strands a strip, and a closed runway can be reopened at any time.

Actions: a controller reads the allocation register; a controller whose read still matches
pulls a strip from the rack and ticks the register; a controller discards a read the
register has moved past; a controller posts the strip in its hand at an open runway; a
controller racks the strip in its hand again; a completed movement returns a posted strip
to the rack; a runway with nothing posted at it is closed; a closed runway is reopened.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The strips racked in the bay, plus the strips posted at the left and
right runways, plus the strips in controllers' hands always add up to the shift's total
strip count, so no allocation, stale-read retry, or runway closure ever creates or loses a
strip.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Any strip a controller is holding eventually leaves that controller's
hand, so no controller stands holding a strip forever.

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m8p3t4 --------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Banks, SlotCount

Slots == 1..SlotCount
FreeLock == "freeLock"
Unallocated == "unallocated"
NoSlot == 0

VARIABLES batchLock, slotLock, ledger, holds, activeSlots

vars == <<batchLock, slotLock, ledger, holds, activeSlots>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ batchLock \in Banks \cup {FreeLock}
    /\ slotLock \in [Slots -> Banks \cup {FreeLock}]
    /\ ledger \in [Slots -> Banks \cup {Unallocated}]
    /\ holds \in [Banks -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ activeSlots \subseteq Slots

Init ==
    /\ batchLock = FreeLock
    /\ slotLock = [s \in Slots |-> FreeLock]
    /\ ledger = [s \in Slots |-> Unallocated]
    /\ holds = [b \in Banks |-> NoSlot]
    /\ activeSlots = Slots

TakeBatchLock(b) ==
    /\ batchLock = FreeLock
    /\ batchLock' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, ledger, holds, activeSlots>>

TakeSlotLock(b, s) ==
    /\ batchLock = b
    /\ s \in activeSlots
    /\ slotLock[s] = FreeLock
    /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![s] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, ledger, holds, activeSlots>>

AllocateSlot(b, s) ==
    /\ batchLock = b
    /\ slotLock[s] = b
    /\ s \in activeSlots
    /\ ledger[s] = Unallocated
    /\ holds[b] = NoSlot
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![s] = b]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![b] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, slotLock, activeSlots>>

DropAllLocks(b) ==
    /\ batchLock = b
    /\ batchLock' = FreeLock
    /\ slotLock' = [s \in Slots |-> IF slotLock[s] = b THEN FreeLock ELSE slotLock[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, holds, activeSlots>>

GiveBackSlot(b) ==
    /\ holds[b] # NoSlot
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![holds[b]] = Unallocated]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![b] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, slotLock, activeSlots>>

AddSlot(s) ==
    /\ s \notin activeSlots
    /\ activeSlots' = activeSlots \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, slotLock, ledger, holds>>

WithdrawSlot(s) ==
    /\ s \in activeSlots
    /\ ledger[s] = Unallocated
    /\ slotLock[s] = FreeLock
    /\ activeSlots' = activeSlots \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, slotLock, ledger, holds>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Banks : TakeBatchLock(b) \/ DropAllLocks(b) \/ GiveBackSlot(b)
    \/ \E b \in Banks, s \in Slots : TakeSlotLock(b, s) \/ AllocateSlot(b, s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : AddSlot(s) \/ WithdrawSlot(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

HeldSlotsMatchLedger ==
    \A b \in Banks : holds[b] # NoSlot => ledger[holds[b]] = b
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Banks = {bnkOne, bnkTwo}
    SlotCount = 2
INVARIANT HeldSlotsMatchLedger
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch divides its settlement window into numbered slots, and
each participating bank may be allocated one slot to push its payments through. A slot
belongs to at most one bank: two banks allocated the same slot would collide on the rail.

Allocation is protected by two levels of lock, coarse before fine. A bank first takes the
batch lock, which covers the whole window, and only while it holds the batch lock may it
take the lock on an individual slot. Unlike a hand-over-hand scheme, the batch lock is
held throughout: a bank keeps both locks until it drops them together, releasing the batch
lock and every slot lock standing in its name in one step.

Holding both the batch lock and a particular slot's lock, and having no slot allocated to
it yet, a bank may allocate that slot: the window's allocation ledger records the slot as
the bank's, and the bank records that it holds that slot. The allocation is refused if the
ledger already shows the slot as somebody's. A bank gives a slot back by clearing both the
ledger entry and its own record together.

The window's capacity changes while the batch runs: slots are added to the window when the
rail widens, and slots are withdrawn when it narrows. A slot may only be withdrawn while
it is unallocated and unlocked, so withdrawing capacity never pulls a slot out from under
a bank.

Actions: a bank takes the free batch lock; a bank holding the batch lock takes the free
lock on an active slot; a bank holding both locks allocates an unallocated active slot to
itself; a bank drops the batch lock and all of its slot locks together; a bank gives back
the slot allocated to it; a slot is added to the window; an unallocated, unlocked slot is
withdrawn from the window.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a bank records that it holds a slot, the window's allocation
ledger shows that same slot as allocated to that same bank, so no slot is ever handed to
two banks at once.

------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m7p1t5 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS MaxVersion, LogLimit

Agents == {"agentEast", "agentWest"}
Machines == {"kioskOne", "kioskTwo"}
NoMachine == "noMachine"
NoRead == [mc |-> NoMachine, saw |-> 0]

VARIABLES version, auditLog, carrying, lockedOut

vars == <<version, auditLog, carrying, lockedOut>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in [Machines -> 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ auditLog \in [Machines -> Seq(0..MaxVersion)]
    /\ carrying \in [Agents -> [mc : Machines \cup {NoMachine}, saw : 0..MaxVersion]]
    /\ lockedOut \subseteq Machines

Init ==
    /\ version = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ auditLog = [m \in Machines |-> << >>]
    /\ carrying = [a \in Agents |-> NoRead]
    /\ lockedOut = {}

ReadVersion(a, m) ==
    /\ carrying[a] = NoRead
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![a] = [mc |-> m, saw |-> version[m]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, auditLog, lockedOut>>

SwapAccepted(a) ==
    /\ carrying[a] # NoRead
    /\ LET m == carrying[a].mc IN
       /\ m \notin lockedOut
       /\ version[m] = carrying[a].saw
       /\ version[m] < MaxVersion
       /\ Len(auditLog[m]) < LogLimit
       /\ auditLog' = [auditLog EXCEPT ![m] = Append(@, carrying[a].saw)]
       /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![a] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED lockedOut

SwapMisses(a) ==
    /\ carrying[a] # NoRead
    /\ \/ carrying[a].mc \in lockedOut
       \/ version[carrying[a].mc] # carrying[a].saw
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![a] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, auditLog, lockedOut>>

AbandonReading(a) ==
    /\ carrying[a] # NoRead
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![a] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, auditLog, lockedOut>>

OperatorForces(m) ==
    /\ m \in lockedOut
    /\ version[m] < MaxVersion
    /\ Len(auditLog[m]) < LogLimit
    /\ auditLog' = [auditLog EXCEPT ![m] = Append(@, version[m])]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carrying, lockedOut>>

LockMachine(m) ==
    /\ m \notin lockedOut
    /\ lockedOut' = lockedOut \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, auditLog, carrying>>

UnlockMachine(m) ==
    /\ m \in lockedOut
    /\ lockedOut' = lockedOut \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, auditLog, carrying>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Agents, m \in Machines : ReadVersion(a, m)
    \/ \E a \in Agents : SwapAccepted(a) \/ SwapMisses(a) \/ AbandonReading(a)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : OperatorForces(m) \/ LockMachine(m) \/ UnlockMachine(m)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(AbandonReading("agentEast"))
    /\ WF_vars(AbandonReading("agentWest"))

AuditLogsAreContiguous ==
    \A m \in Machines :
        \A i \in 1..Len(auditLog[m]) : auditLog[m][i] = i - 1

ReadingsAreLetGo ==
    \A a \in Agents : (carrying[a] # NoRead) ~> (carrying[a] = NoRead)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    MaxVersion = 2
    LogLimit = 2
INVARIANT AuditLogsAreContiguous
PROPERTY ReadingsAreLetGo
nl:
A vending machine network keeps a price record for every machine. Each machine's record
carries a version number, and beside it the machine keeps an audit log: one entry per
accepted price change, recording the version that change was written on top of.

Field pricing agents amend prices through a compare-and-swap. An agent reads a machine's
version and carries that reading around. When it comes to write, the swap is accepted only
if the machine's version is still exactly what the agent read; accepting appends the read
version to the machine's audit log and ticks the machine's version by one. If the version
has moved on since the read, the swap misses and the agent throws the reading away. An
agent may also simply abandon a reading it is carrying and walk away from it.

The network operator has a privileged admin override. The operator can lock a machine,
which shuts field agents out of it entirely: while a machine is locked no agent swap is
accepted there. On a locked machine the operator can force a price straight in without
reading anything first, and that forced write is logged exactly like an agent's, recording
the version it went in on top of and ticking the version. The operator unlocks the machine
afterwards.

A machine's audit log is only so long; once it is full no further change, agent or
operator, is accepted on that machine.

Actions: an agent reads a machine's version; an agent's swap is accepted, logging the read
version and ticking the machine; an agent's swap misses because the version moved or the
machine is locked; an agent abandons the reading it carries; the operator forces a write
into a locked machine, logging and ticking it; the operator locks a machine; the operator
unlocks a machine.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every machine's audit log reads as a gapless, repeat-free run of
versions -- its first entry went in on version zero, its second on version one, and so on
-- so no accepted change was ever written on top of a version that another change had
already built on.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every version reading an agent is carrying is eventually let go of, so
no agent holds an unresolved reading forever.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Forklifts, LeaseLife, MaxCredits

Vans == {"vanNorthOne", "vanNorthTwo", "vanSouthOne"}
Fleets == {"fleetNorth", "fleetSouth"}
FleetOf == [vanNorthOne |-> "fleetNorth", vanNorthTwo |-> "fleetNorth",
            vanSouthOne |-> "fleetSouth"]

VARIABLES lease, loading, asking, credits

vars == <<lease, loading, asking, credits>>

Leased == {v \in Vans : lease[v] > 0}

TypeOK ==
    /\ lease \in [Vans -> 0..LeaseLife]
    /\ loading \subseteq Vans
    /\ asking \subseteq Vans
    /\ credits \in [Fleets -> 0..MaxCredits]

Init ==
    /\ lease = [v \in Vans |-> 0]
    /\ loading = {}
    /\ asking = {}
    /\ credits = [f \in Fleets |-> 0]

AskForLease(v) ==
    /\ v \notin asking
    /\ lease[v] = 0
    /\ asking' = asking \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, loading, credits>>

GrantLease(v) ==
    /\ v \in asking
    /\ lease[v] = 0
    /\ Cardinality(Leased) < Forklifts
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![v] = LeaseLife]
    /\ asking' = asking \ {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loading, credits>>

StartLoading(v) ==
    /\ lease[v] > 0
    /\ v \notin loading
    /\ loading' = loading \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, asking, credits>>

FinishLoading(v) ==
    /\ v \in loading
    /\ credits[FleetOf[v]] < MaxCredits
    /\ loading' = loading \ {v}
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![v] = 0]
    /\ credits' = [credits EXCEPT ![FleetOf[v]] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED asking

CountdownTicks(v) ==
    /\ lease[v] > 1
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![v] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loading, asking, credits>>

LeaseRunsOut(v) ==
    /\ lease[v] = 1
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![v] = 0]
    /\ loading' = loading \ {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<asking, credits>>

RenewLease(v) ==
    /\ lease[v] > 0
    /\ lease[v] < LeaseLife
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![v] = LeaseLife]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loading, asking, credits>>

ShipRestock(f) ==
    /\ credits[f] > 0
    /\ credits' = [credits EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, loading, asking>>

Next ==
    \/ \E v \in Vans :
           \/ AskForLease(v) \/ GrantLease(v) \/ StartLoading(v) \/ FinishLoading(v)
           \/ CountdownTicks(v) \/ LeaseRunsOut(v) \/ RenewLease(v)
    \/ \E f \in Fleets : ShipRestock(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DepotStaysWithinForklifts ==
    Cardinality({v \in Vans : lease[v] > 0 \/ v \in loading}) <= Forklifts
