SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Forklifts = 2
    LeaseLife = 2
    MaxCredits = 2
INVARIANT DepotStaysWithinForklifts
nl:
A vending machine network is restocked by two independent operator fleets that happen to
share one depot. The fleets plan their own routes and know nothing of each other; the only
thing they contend for is the depot's forklifts, of which there are fewer than there are
vans. A van can only be loaded while it is on a forklift, so the forklifts are the depot's
hard capacity.

The depot hands out forklift leases rather than locks. A van asks for a lease, and the
depot grants one only while the number of live leases is still below the forklift count.
A lease is not open-ended: it carries a countdown that ticks down on its own. A van that
is still loading renews its lease, which puts the countdown back to full. If a countdown
runs all the way out, the lease is gone and the depot fences that van off the forklift in
the same step, whether or not the van thought it was still loading -- an expired lease
never leaves a van standing on a forklift.

A van that holds a live lease starts loading, and when it finishes it comes off the
forklift and the restock is credited to whichever fleet the van belongs to. Credited
restocks are shipped out to the machines afterwards.

Actions: a van asks the depot for a lease; the depot grants a lease while it is below the
forklift count; a van holding a lease starts loading on a forklift; a loading van finishes
and its restock is credited to its fleet; a lease countdown ticks down; a lease runs out,
fencing its van off the forklift; a van renews its lease; a fleet ships out a credited
restock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of vans that either hold a live forklift lease or are standing
on a forklift never exceeds the depot's forklift count, no matter which fleet the vans
belong to.

Phones == {"phoneAda", "phoneBen", "phoneCleo"}

Pending == {p \in Phones : queued[p] # NoCommand}

    /\ generation \in 0..MaxGeneration
    /\ believes \in [Phones -> 0..MaxGeneration]
    /\ queued \in [Phones -> 0..(MaxGeneration + 1)]
    /\ admitted \subseteq Phones

    /\ generation = 0
    /\ believes = [p \in Phones |-> 0]
    /\ queued = [p \in Phones |-> NoCommand]
    /\ admitted = {}

RotateGeneration ==
    /\ generation < MaxGeneration
    /\ generation' = generation + 1
    /\ admitted' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<believes, queued>>

SyncPhone(p) ==
    /\ believes[p] # generation
    /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![p] = generation]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<generation, queued, admitted>>

    /\ Cardinality(Pending) < QueueCap

HubThrowsOff(p) ==

    /\ \/ queued[p] # generation
       \/ believes[p] # generation
    /\ queued' = [queued EXCEPT ![p] = NoCommand]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<generation, believes, admitted>>

PhoneLeaves(p) ==

    /\ admitted' = admitted \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<generation, believes, queued>>

Next ==
    \/ RotateGeneration
    \/ \E p \in Phones :

Spec ==

    /\ WF_vars(HubAdmits("phoneAda") \/ HubThrowsOff("phoneAda"))
    /\ WF_vars(HubAdmits("phoneBen") \/ HubThrowsOff("phoneBen"))
    /\ WF_vars(HubAdmits("phoneCleo") \/ HubThrowsOff("phoneCleo"))

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    MaxGeneration = 2
    QueueCap = 2
INVARIANT AdmittedPhonesAreCurrent
PROPERTY QueueAlwaysDrains
nl:
A smart-home door lock network admits residents' phones through a hub. Credentials are
issued in numbered generations; the household rotates the credential generation whenever
somebody is removed from the home, which bumps the generation by one and immediately turns
every phone currently admitted back out. A phone learns the current generation by syncing
with the hub, and carries whatever generation it last learned.

A phone asks to be let in by putting an unlock command on the hub's command queue. The
command carries the generation the phone believes in at the time it is queued. The queue
is bounded and applies backpressure: while it is full, no further command is accepted onto
it, and a phone has at most one command queued at a time.

The radio between the phones and the hub gives no ordering guarantee, so the hub does not
work the queue in arrival order. It picks whichever queued command it likes. A command is
acted on only if the generation it carries is the household's current generation and the
phone that sent it is itself synced to that generation; acting on it admits the phone.
Any other queued command -- one carrying a generation the household has rotated past, or
sent by a phone that has not caught up -- is thrown off the queue without being acted on.
An admitted phone leaves the house and is no longer admitted.

Actions: the household rotates the credential generation, turning out everyone admitted; a
phone syncs its generation with the hub; a phone queues an unlock command carrying its
believed generation, while the queue has room; the hub acts on a queued command whose
generation is current and whose phone is synced, admitting that phone; the hub throws any
other queued command off the queue; an admitted phone leaves.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every phone that is currently admitted to the house is synced to the
household's current credential generation, so no phone on a rotated-past credential is
ever inside.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every unlock command that reaches the hub's queue eventually leaves it,
so no command sits queued forever without being acted on or thrown off.

Slots == 1..SlotCount

    /\ holdsSlot = [g \in Guests |-> NoSlot]
    /\ jobSlot = [g \in Guests |-> NoSlot]
    /\ jobBy = [g \in Guests |-> NoSystem]

cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    SlotCount = 2
    QueueCap = 1
INVARIANT GuestSlotsMatchTheLock
nl:
A smart-home door lock network keeps a small pool of guest key slots on each door, and two
completely independent systems provision them: the manufacturer's cloud service and the
household's local hub. Neither knows what the other is doing; they both simply push
provisioning jobs at the same lock, for the same pool of slots. A slot may hold at most one
guest's key -- two guests provisioned into the same slot would overwrite each other's key.

Provisioning goes through the lock's job queue, which is bounded and applies backpressure:
while the queue is full no further job is accepted from either system, and a guest has at
most one job outstanding. A job names the guest, the slot the queuing system believes is
free, and which of the two systems queued it. Because the two systems do not coordinate,
a job may well name a slot that is no longer free by the time the lock gets to it.

The lock is the only serialiser. It applies a job only if the slot the job names is still
genuinely free on the lock and the guest named does not already hold a slot; applying it
writes the guest into that slot, records on the guest's side which slot it got, and
credits the provisioning to the system that queued it. Any job that does not still hold up
-- naming a slot that has since been taken, or a guest that has since been provisioned
elsewhere -- is thrown off the queue unapplied. A guest's access can be revoked, which
frees the slot again.

Actions: one of the two systems queues a provisioning job for a guest and a slot while the
queue has room; the lock applies a job whose slot is still free and whose guest holds no
slot; the lock throws off a job that no longer holds up; a guest's access is revoked and
its slot freed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a guest is recorded as holding a slot, that slot on the lock
holds that same guest's key, so no slot is ever provisioned to two guests at once.

---- MODULE W4Od11m7p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Stations, Capacity, MaxVersion

Slack == Capacity + 1
NoRead == [cnt |-> -1, ver |-> -1]

VARIABLES reg, readOf, rush, seized

vars == <<reg, readOf, rush, seized>>

Reads == {NoRead} \union [cnt : 0..Slack, ver : 0..MaxVersion]

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [cnt : 0..Slack, ver : 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ readOf \in [Stations -> Reads]
    /\ rush \in 0..Slack
    /\ seized \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ reg = [cnt |-> 0, ver |-> 0]
    /\ readOf = [w \in Stations |-> NoRead]
    /\ rush = 0
    /\ seized = FALSE

ReadRegister(w) ==
    /\ readOf[w] = NoRead
    /\ readOf' = [readOf EXCEPT ![w] = reg]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, rush, seized>>

CasEnqueue(w) ==
    /\ readOf[w] # NoRead
    /\ readOf[w].ver = reg.ver
    /\ ~seized
    /\ reg.cnt + rush + 1 <= Capacity
    /\ reg.ver < MaxVersion
    /\ reg' = [cnt |-> reg.cnt + 1, ver |-> reg.ver + 1]
    /\ readOf' = [readOf EXCEPT ![w] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rush, seized>>

DiscardStaleRead(w) ==
    /\ readOf[w] # NoRead
    /\ readOf[w].ver # reg.ver
    /\ readOf' = [readOf EXCEPT ![w] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, rush, seized>>

SeizeSpooler ==
    /\ ~seized
    /\ seized' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, readOf, rush>>

ReleaseSpooler ==
    /\ seized
    /\ seized' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, readOf, rush>>

InjectRush ==
    /\ seized
    /\ reg.cnt + rush + 1 <= Capacity
    /\ rush' = rush + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, readOf, seized>>

PrintNormal ==
    /\ reg.cnt > 0
    /\ reg.ver < MaxVersion
    /\ reg' = [cnt |-> reg.cnt - 1, ver |-> reg.ver + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readOf, rush, seized>>

PrintRush ==
    /\ rush > 0
    /\ rush' = rush - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, readOf, seized>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Stations : ReadRegister(w)
    \/ \E w \in Stations : CasEnqueue(w)
    \/ \E w \in Stations : DiscardStaleRead(w)
    \/ SeizeSpooler
    \/ ReleaseSpooler
    \/ InjectRush
    \/ PrintNormal
    \/ PrintRush

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SpoolWithinCapacity == reg.cnt + rush <= Capacity

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Stations = {w1, w2}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxVersion = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT SpoolWithinCapacity
nl:
A print shop job spooler shares one physical spool of fixed capacity between a
normal lane and a priority lane. The spool's occupancy is published in a single
compare-and-swap register that carries the normal lane's job count together
with a version stamp that is bumped on every successful write.

A workstation that wants to queue a job first reads the register, keeping the
count and version it saw. It then attempts a compare-and-swap: the attempt only
lands if the version it read is still the register's current version, if the
shop administrator has not seized the spooler, and if adding one more job would
still leave the normal lane plus the priority lane within the spool's total
capacity. A workstation whose read has gone stale, because the version no
longer matches, simply discards its read and starts over.

The shop administrator has a privileged override. The administrator can seize
the spooler, which blocks all compare-and-swap traffic, and can release it
again. While holding the seizure the administrator injects rush jobs directly
into the priority lane, bypassing the register protocol entirely, but the
administrator is still required to leave the two lanes together within the
spool's total capacity. The press pulls work off either lane: printing a normal
job decrements the register's count and bumps its version, and printing a rush
job decrements the priority lane.

The complete set of actions is: read the register, compare-and-swap a normal
job into the spool, discard a stale read, seize the spooler as administrator,
release the seizure, inject a rush job into the priority lane, print a normal
job, and print a rush job.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of normal jobs recorded in the register plus the
number of rush jobs in the priority lane never exceeds the spool's total
capacity, no matter how compare-and-swap retries and administrator injections
interleave.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m9p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Presses, Jobs, MaxEpoch

NoJob == "nojob"

VARIABLES epoch, config, learned, holding, pool

vars == <<epoch, config, learned, holding, pool>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ config \subseteq Presses
    /\ learned \in [Presses -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ holding \in [Presses -> Jobs \union {NoJob}]
    /\ pool \subseteq Jobs

Evict(newCfg) == [p \in Presses |-> IF p \in newCfg THEN holding[p] ELSE NoJob]

Reclaimed(newCfg) ==
    {holding[p] : p \in {q \in Presses : q \notin newCfg /\ holding[q] # NoJob}}

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ config = Presses
    /\ learned = [p \in Presses |-> 0]
    /\ holding = [p \in Presses |-> NoJob]
    /\ pool = Jobs

Reconfigure(newCfg) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ newCfg # config
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ config' = newCfg
    /\ holding' = Evict(newCfg)
    /\ pool' = pool \union Reclaimed(newCfg)
    /\ UNCHANGED learned

LearnEpoch(p) ==
    /\ learned[p] # epoch
    /\ learned' = [learned EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, holding, pool>>

TakeJob(p, j) ==
    /\ p \in config
    /\ learned[p] = epoch
    /\ holding[p] = NoJob
    /\ j \in pool
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![p] = j]
    /\ pool' = pool \ {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, learned>>

FinishPrint(p) ==
    /\ holding[p] # NoJob
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![p] = NoJob]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, learned, pool>>

HandBack(p) ==
    /\ holding[p] # NoJob
    /\ pool' = pool \union {holding[p]}
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![p] = NoJob]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, learned>>

AdminInstallConfig(newCfg) ==
    /\ newCfg # config
    /\ config' = newCfg
    /\ holding' = Evict(newCfg)
    /\ pool' = pool \union Reclaimed(newCfg)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, learned>>

AdminHandJob(p, j) ==
    /\ p \in config
    /\ holding[p] = NoJob
    /\ j \in pool
    /\ holding' = [holding EXCEPT ![p] = j]
    /\ pool' = pool \ {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, learned>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in SUBSET Presses : Reconfigure(c)
    \/ \E p \in Presses : LearnEpoch(p)
    \/ \E p \in Presses, j \in Jobs : TakeJob(p, j)
    \/ \E p \in Presses : FinishPrint(p)
    \/ \E p \in Presses : HandBack(p)
    \/ \E c \in SUBSET Presses : AdminInstallConfig(c)
    \/ \E p \in Presses, j \in Jobs : AdminHandJob(p, j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OnlyAuthorisedPressHoldsJob ==
    \A p \in Presses : holding[p] # NoJob => p \in config

====
nl:
A print shop job spooler decides which presses are in service using
epoch-numbered reconfiguration. The shop holds a current configuration, which is
the set of presses authorised to take work, and an epoch number that advances
every time the configuration is changed through the normal path. Each press
separately remembers the epoch it last learned. Jobs waiting for a press sit in
a pool.

A normal reconfiguration advances the epoch and installs a new set of authorised
presses. Any press dropped by the new configuration immediately gives up the job
it was holding, and that job goes back into the waiting pool, so a press that has
just lost its authorisation is never left running work. A press can learn the
current epoch at any time.

A press takes a job out of the pool only when it is in the current configuration
and the epoch it has learned is the current epoch; a press whose learned epoch is
behind has to catch up first. A press holding a job can finish printing it, which
frees the press. A press can also hand a job back to the pool unfinished.

The shop administrator has a privileged override with two powers. The
administrator can install a new configuration directly, without advancing the
epoch at all, and this override still drops the jobs of any press it removes from
the configuration. The administrator can also hand a waiting job straight to a
press, skipping the epoch check entirely, but only to a press that is in the
current configuration.

The complete set of actions is: reconfigure normally with an epoch advance, let a
press learn the current epoch, take a job from the pool as an up-to-date
authorised press, finish printing a held job, hand a held job back to the pool,
install a configuration by administrator override without an epoch advance, and
hand a job directly to an authorised press by administrator override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every press that is holding a job is a member of the current
configuration, so no press that reconfiguration has stripped of its authorisation
is ever left holding shop work.
